title: Median product "lifespan" has fallen from ~4y down to ~1.5y
summary:
The "product graveyard" of SaaSHub has been tracking the status (and lifespan) of hundreds of thousands of products. It's been hovering around 4y for quite some time. However, there's a sharp decline in 2026 leading to about 1.5y these days. https://www.saashub.com/product-graveyard That's a huge drop. And, it matches my "human" observations. A lot of products are being vibe coded, released, and soon after that abandoned. It's become too cheap to produce software. So, a lot of people have been experimenting for 'free' with their ideas - only to find out that they weren't viable... or that they couldn't bring customers in. Distribution and marketing have become much more important than before - within the context that everyone can build "features" for free.

Anyhow, I expect this trend of shortening product lifespan to continue even further down. Or maybe, at some point people will realised that there are no users for their products as every user can "build" their own and custom product. Leaving us with a dozen huge platforms that host and help you build those apps. Until then - it's a crazy gold rush and a lot of makers are abandoning their empty buckets.

title: GitHub now uses a generic avatar instead of "Identicons" for new profiles
summary:
I couldn't fit a better explanation in the title, it affects all users who don't upload a custom profile picture, not just new accounts. A lot of people, myself included, just use(d) the default Identicon[1] (random-ish generated pixel art, basically). The new avatar is a grey rounded GitHub logo.

I noticed this just now after restarting VSCode and seeing my avatar look different. On the website, the top right account button still uses the Identicon for me, but changing any URL parameter of the image shows the new generic avatar, so I suspect it's just cached on their CDN.

I found a discussion[2] on GitHub about this, some people in there see it as a sign of an impending ban, I highly doubt this is the case here, since browsing any large-ish list of users anywhere on the website shows no Identicons and a lot of the new generic profile picture.

The GitHub changelog[3] doesn't list anything (yet).

[1] More context about what Identicons are: https://github.blog/news-insights/company-news/identicons/

[2] https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/211045

[3] https://github.blog/changelog/

Relevant Reddit thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/github/comments/1xcxbup/github_profile_picture_reset/

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50202403

title: UPDATE: Anthropic's non-existant customer support
summary:
I know most people here are likely power users with ample token budgets but I am not. I use claude-cli (the 22$/€ plan) for code in thesis related work in varying ways and a reset I had banked (valid until today) vanished from my account without warning or explanation (not even a history of resets or similar). I thought this would be an easy fix but somehow the support agent can see every usage stat and reset time I have but that one. It refuses to escalate the issue to someone who can help and I started looking here and on reddit and it appears this is a common issue. How is this acceptable to any community's standard and is there a specific way people deal with this? The only other option I feel is to bare our collective throats to AI companies who we pay to then beg for not arbitrary altering deals.

I know this is a rant in many ways but I am wondering if people share in this feeling or are generally just content with the status quo?

UPDATE: Threatening will result in human response but not a helpful, nor personalized one. Even the links like " Reply directly to this email or through our Messenger" do not work. If anyone ever needs to reach Anthropic human support I do not think it is morally reprehensive to do so by threatening an unhelpful service AI, if you do that's fine. It works however.

title: Tell HN: Claude resets expire at an arbitrary time during deadline day
summary:
I was saving a reset on Claude until today and maximising my usage because of it, i.e. I'm almost out of tokens.

When I went to use my reset this afternoon (which was listed as expiring on the 22nd Oct), it said it was no longer valid as it had expired, despite still being in a window I had opened this morning and it still being the 22nd.

I asked support and a very nice Claude explained they didn't do human support and they don't do resets so I was shit out of luck.

Bearing in mind I pay £900 a year for the product, I thought I might get a little more leeway, but there you go.

Tomorrow when I run out of tokens I'll be checking out the competition on OpenRouter, which seems like an own goal on Anthropic's part.

PSA: Claude resets expire at some point before they say they do, and there is no support.

title: Ask HN: Should AI be making decisions, or just make sure you see what matters?
summary:
Everyone is rushing to develop an “AI chief of staff” which replaces the human role entirely. But I feel like that’s taking the wrong perspective altogether. Decisions must remain human-made. The thing that’s missing is timely, relevant information.

Right now, leadership has to hop through multiple dashboards, lengthy slides or pdf documents, and platforms trying to find the context of reality of a situation. Each platform holds some data and nobody ever pulls information from all of them. In addition, LLMs mean starting from zero every time – explaining the background context, teaching skills and configuring MCP before you can start doing something.

We are working on something better. Connect your tools (CRM, Slack, calls, issue tracker), and we’ll keep track of all the context and changes for you. We’ll monitor external environment as well – news, filings, events on your customers and your own profile, competition. When something important happens, you’ll get notified and links to the sources. Otherwise, it remains silent and let you focus on the decisions – while we handle everything else.

We are early in development and discovery process ourselves, so please share your thoughts with us:

Do you face this problem too? How do you handle it today? What would make you wary of a tool like this? Would you use it once it’s ready?

If you’d like to be part of the journey, comment below or email me at rearviewmine@gmail.com :)
